g1_loop#3.closest: Standard addition method (analytical chemistry, long-established; spike known amounts, regress response, extrapolate to zero) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_addition ; LLMORPH: Automated Metamorphic Testing of Large Language Models (2026) https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23611 (also Yee et al. error-injection recovery tests on chain of thought, found via search but not opened)
g1_loop#3.new: what is genuinely new, in one sentence: Using standard-addition-style slope and zero-spike extrapolation on live LLM tasks as a bias corrector, with recovery-triggered adapter creation and deletion; I found no LLM paper that does this, though the individual pieces (known-effect perturbations, injected-fact recovery) exist.

g1_core#3.closest: Turbo principle and EXIT charts for iterative decoding (ten Brink-era comms theory, e.g. Southampton EXIT chart paper) https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/383511 ; When and Why Does Multi-Agent Debate Fail and Does It Really Underperform? g1_core#3.new: what is genuinely new, in one sentence: Porting extrinsic-only LLR exchange across an interleaver between two differently ordered reasoning chains scored against parity-like constraints, with per-problem-type EXIT curves used to abstain; the decoding machinery is classical, and I found no LLM version of it.

g1_core#1.closest: Baarda data snooping and reliability/redundancy theory in geodetic least-squares adjustment (1968/1977; review "A half century of Baarda's concept of reliability" https://agrimensura.florianopolis.ifsc.edu.br/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/A-half-century-of-Baarda-s-concept-of-reliability-a-review-new-perspectives-and-applications.pdf) ; ConCoRD: Enhancing Self-Consistency and Performance of Pre-Trained Language Models through Natural Language Inference (2022) https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11875 (also Belief Tree Propagation (2025) https://arxiv.org/html/2406.06950v2)
g1_core#1.new: what is genuinely new, in one sentence: Applying closed-loop weighted least-squares misclosure spreading, normalized-residual blunder naming, and per-claim redundancy numbers (near-zero means structurally unverifiable) to an LLM's own quantitative claims, whereas existing LLM work uses MaxSAT or tree/factor-graph inference without redundancy or reliability measures.

g1_core#2.closest: Desroziers et al., Diagnosis of observation, background and analysis error statistics in observation space (2005) https://bibliotheque.meteo.fr/pub/DOC00017306-diagnosis-observation-background-and-analysis-erro.html ; Knowledge-Based Trust: Estimating the Trustworthiness of Web Sources (2015) https://arxiv.org/pdf/1502.03519 (Kalman-style LLM work: Filtering Beats Fine-Tuning: A Bayesian Kalman View of In-Context Learning (2026) https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06100v1)
g1_core#2.new: what is genuinely new, in one sentence: Using Desroziers identities as label-free estimators of per-source and per-model-region error covariance to set the gain for both belief and parameter updates in an LLM-like system; data assimilation and unsupervised source-reliability estimation each exist, and the Kalman-LLM papers I found use labels or a different formulation.
